name: Kish
overview: Kish was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, noted in Scripture as a mighty man of valor, which may also imply wealth or influence. His prominence is briefly highlighted without extensive narrative detail. There are no additional notes expanding on his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Kish means "bow" or "power," reflecting a possible symbolism of strength or skill, as indicated in 1 Samuel 9:1. This proper name was not given by God but holds significance in identifying him within the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Kish is recorded as the grandson of Abiel and the father of Saul, the first king of Israel. He is also identified as the father of Ner. These relationships establish his place within a notable lineage in the tribe of Benjamin.
scriptureSignificance: Kish's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his role as the father of Saul, Israel's first king, linking him directly to a pivotal moment in Israel's history. His description as a mighty man of valor suggests a man of standing and influence within his tribe, setting the stage for Saul's rise. Although not extensively detailed, Kish's lineage and status provide foundational context for understanding Saul's background and the early monarchy.
